_meta.indication: Treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults
_meta.receipt_date: March 30, 2022 (original BLA); standard resubmission received May 24, 2023

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 induction study, evaluated up to 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled induction study; subjects randomized 3:1 to 300 mg OMVOH or placebo by IV infusion at Weeks 0, 4, and 8
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis with inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to conventional or biologic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: clinical remission at Week 12
pivotal_trials.n: 1062 subjects evaluated for efficacy (randomized 3:1 to OMVOH or placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical remission at Week 12: 24% OMVOH (N=795) vs 15% placebo (N=267); treatment difference 10% (95% CI 5, 15), p<0.001

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 maintenance study, treatment up to 52 weeks total
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized withdrawal, double-blind, placebo-controlled maintenance study; Week-12 responders randomized 2:1 to 200 mg OMVOH or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 40 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis who achieved clinical response at Week 12 in UC-1
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: clinical remission at Week 40
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical remission at Week 40: 51% OMVOH (N=337) vs 27% placebo (N=169); treatment difference 22% (95% CI 14, 31)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%): induction - upper respiratory tract infections (8% vs 6% placebo) and arthralgia (2% vs 1%); maintenance - upper respiratory tract infections (14% vs 12%), injection site reactions (9% vs 4%), arthralgia (7% vs 4%), rash (4% vs 1%), headache (4% vs 1%), and herpes viral infection (2% vs 1%). Hepatotoxicity and infections are warnings.
target_moa: Interleukin-23 antagonist: a humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of human IL-23 and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor, thereby inhibiting release of pro-inflammatory cytokines involved in mucosal inflammation

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a biologic of this class

summary.text: OMVOH was reviewed under the standard (non-priority) review track as a standard resubmission after the original BLA received a Complete Response Letter for manufacturing facility deficiencies; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, priority review, or advisory committee. The program held an Orphan Drug Designation for pediatric ulcerative colitis (exempting it from PREA), while approval was granted for adults.

requirement.text: 4409-2 Conduct a prospective, registry-based, observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to mirikizumab-containing products regardless of indication during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 4409-2 Conduct a prospective, registry-based, observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to mirikizumab-containing products regardless of indication during pregnancy to an unexposed control population. The registry should be designed to detect and record major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, small for gestational age births, preterm births, and any other adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, neonatal deaths, and infections, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4409-4 Conduct an observational study to assess the incidence of severe acute liver injury in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis who are exposed to Omvoh (mirikizumab-mrkz), relative to other therapies used to treat ulcerative colitis.

citations.quote: 4409-4 Conduct an observational study to assess the incidence of severe acute liver injury in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis who are exposed to Omvoh (mirikizumab-mrkz), relative to other therapies used to treat ulcerative colitis. Compare rates (per person-time) or risks (proportion of patients with a minimum amount of follow-up). Describe and justify the choice of appropriate comparator population(s). Specify concise case definition for severe liver injury and validation of algorithm(s) to identify severe liver injury in the proposed data source. For the Omvoh (mirikizumab-mrkz)-exposed and comparator(s) cohorts, clearly define the study drug initiation period and any exclusion and inclusion criteria. Ensure that the data source allows for average follow-up for at least 1 year. Specify a minimum sample size and justify the precision of the estimate achievable with the proposed study.
